name: Wormhole
summary: A forged guardian verification path let the attacker mint wrapped ETH on Solana without a valid guardian message.
root: Guardian signature verification/account validation failure involving instruction sysvar validation path.
root_cause: The program accepted a verification-looking instruction/account path without fully binding the sysvar, verifier program, guardian signatures, and payload.
exploit_path: Forge the verification precondition, submit a malicious VAA, and mint wrapped assets against an invalid message.
takeaway: Do not merely check that a verification-looking instruction/account exists; bind sysvar, verifier program, signer, payload, and instruction position.

name: Nomad
summary: A zero trusted root made arbitrary messages appear valid after an upgrade.
root: Bridge replica accepted messages against a zero trusted root.
root_cause: Initialization/configuration allowed the committed root of zero to be treated as an acceptable root for message validation.
exploit_path: Copy a successful transaction, replace recipient/amount fields, and submit arbitrary messages that validated against the zero root.
takeaway: Initialization and trusted-root state are security-critical; test nonzero roots, replay resistance, and invalid-message rejection after upgrades.

name: Ronin
summary: An attacker compromised enough validator keys to satisfy the bridge withdrawal quorum.
root_cause: The bridge security boundary depended on a small validator signer set whose keys and allowlist state were compromised.
exploit_path: Obtain enough validator signatures, authorize fraudulent withdrawals, and drain bridge reserves.
takeaway: Bridge signer sets, allowlists, key custody, threshold size, and emergency controls are part of audit scope even when on-chain verification works as designed.

name: Multichain
summary: Bridge funds were drained after compromise or loss of control of MPC/key infrastructure.
root: MPC/private-key compromise and opaque operational control.
root_cause: The asset custody model concentrated security in off-chain MPC infrastructure and administrative access that users and integrators could not independently verify.
exploit_path: Use compromised signing/control infrastructure to move assets from bridge-controlled addresses.
takeaway: For bridges, document who can sign, pause, upgrade, rotate keys, or move custody assets; smart-contract tests do not cover opaque MPC control risk.

name: Allbridge
summary: Pool pricing and liquidity accounting were manipulated to drain bridge liquidity.
root: Pool invariant and price manipulation in bridge liquidity accounting.
root_cause: The bridge's swap/liquidity pool mechanics let an attacker skew prices and withdraw more value than they supplied.
exploit_path: Manipulate pool balances/prices through swaps and liquidity operations, then withdraw underpriced assets.
takeaway: Bridge liquidity pools need invariant tests and manipulation-cost analysis, not only message-authentication checks.

name: deBridge Solana signature-verification-bypass class
impact: Class-level audit finding; no canonical loss postmortem
summary: Solana bridge programs that rely on instruction introspection can accept forged or unrelated signature-verification instructions if payload, signer, index, and verifier program are not fully bound.
root: Signature verification bypass class in Solana bridge/message verification flows.
root_cause: Programs may check that a signature-verification instruction exists without proving it verified the exact bridge payload for the exact signer and instruction position.
exploit_path: Place a valid-looking Ed25519/secp verification instruction in the transaction, then call the bridge with a different message or account set.
takeaway: When a Solana bridge uses signature instructions, bind verifier program, instruction index, signer, domain, nonce, payload, and all action parameters.

name: LayerZero / Stargate DVN and library configuration
summary: LayerZero-style systems make endpoint libraries, oracle/relayer or DVN sets, confirmations, and per-path configuration part of the security boundary.
root: Bridge security depends on message library and DVN/oracle/relayer configuration, not only application contract code.
root_cause: Applications can inherit weaker-than-expected trust assumptions if send/receive libraries, required DVNs, optional DVNs, thresholds, or confirmations are misconfigured.
exploit_path: Compromise or misconfigure the verification path so a message is accepted under a weaker trust model than the app owner intended.
takeaway: Audit the per-route message library and verifier configuration as protocol state; pin expected endpoints and document who can change them.

name: Cashio
summary: Fake collateral and LP accounts let the attacker mint unbacked CASH.
root: Incomplete collateral/LP/mint account validation allowed fake account chains and infinite CASH minting.
root_cause: The program failed to prove that supplied accounts were the canonical Saber pool, LP mint, token mints, collateral accounts, and related accounts.
exploit_path: Provide counterfeit accounts with compatible fields, satisfy shallow checks, mint unbacked CASH, and swap it for real assets.
takeaway: Valid accounts must also be the right accounts for the mint/pool/collateral chain; this is directly relevant to approval-PDA designs and Kamino/KLend CPI account ordering.

name: Mango Markets
summary: The attacker manipulated a low-liquidity market and oracle-driven collateral value, then borrowed against inflated collateral.
root: Low-liquidity market/oracle/economic manipulation enabled inflated collateral borrowing.
root_cause: Risk parameters and oracle design allowed valid protocol state to reflect an economically manipulated MNGO price.
exploit_path: Use large positions and liquidity to move the mark/oracle price, inflate account equity, borrow assets, and leave bad debt.
takeaway: Economic design, oracle source/liquidity, and flash-loan-style composition are audit scope even when every transaction is valid protocol state.

name: Solend whale liquidation crisis
impact: Bad-debt and governance crisis risk; emergency DAO proposal
summary: A large borrower's position threatened cascading liquidations, oracle/DEX stress, and bad debt.
root_cause: Protocol risk parameters allowed a single account to create liquidation pressure larger than available market liquidity could absorb safely.
exploit_path: Not a conventional exploit; adverse price movement could force liquidations that move markets and create insolvency.
takeaway: Lending audits should include concentration limits, liquidation liquidity, emergency governance powers, and whether privileged intervention can bypass normal controls.

name: Nirvana Finance
summary: Flash-loan liquidity was used to manipulate protocol pricing and drain value.
root: Flash-loan-assisted pricing/economic manipulation of protocol mechanism.
root_cause: The protocol's pricing mechanism could be moved atomically with borrowed liquidity and then traded against for profit.
exploit_path: Borrow large liquidity, skew the price mechanism, buy/redeem or swap against the distorted price, repay the loan, and keep the spread.
takeaway: Check AMM/pricing invariants, manipulation cost, circuit breakers, and atomic composition assumptions.

name: Crema Finance
summary: Fake tick/price accounts enabled a fee-claim path to account for liquidity incorrectly.
root: Fake tick/price account and faulty owner/account validation in concentrated liquidity fee-claim path.
root_cause: A sibling instruction path failed to validate account ownership and relationships for tick/price data.
exploit_path: Provide fake accounts to the vulnerable path, cause incorrect fee accounting, and withdraw value.
takeaway: Audit all instruction variants and helper paths; one correctly validated path does not protect a sibling method.

name: Raydium
summary: Compromised authority keys were used to drain liquidity pools.
root: Compromised admin/owner authority used to drain pools.
root_cause: Privileged key compromise exposed pool-draining authority.
exploit_path: Use compromised authority to call privileged drain paths against pools.
takeaway: Key management, authority blast radius, and emergency/admin powers are part of security review.

name: Slope wallet incident
summary: Wallet/application key handling failure exposed user keys.
root: Wallet/application key handling failure, not a Solana program bug.
root_cause: Private key material was mishandled by wallet infrastructure.
exploit_path: Use exposed key material to sign unauthorized transfers from affected wallets.
takeaway: Classify ecosystem losses correctly; wallet/key custody incidents may be out of smart-contract scope but affect threat model.
